name: Bridge
summary: Contract bridge, kept simple. WOPR deals and bids all four hands, your side always declares, and you play both your hand and dummy's while WOPR defends; one deal is one game.
howToPlay: WOPR bids by point count and shows the auction and the contract, for example CONTRACT: 3NT BY SOUTH. WEST LEADS. If East and West hold more points, WOPR turns the table so that your side declares.
Make the contract: take at least 6 tricks plus its level (3NT needs 9). The contract's suit is trumps; NT has none.
The panel shows North's and South's hands a suit at a time. The > marks the hand to play, and the prompt names it: SOUTH PLAYS: or DUMMY (NORTH) PLAYS:.
Name a card as 7H, 10D or KS. A rank alone (K, 7) also works when it fits one card: the one in the suit led, or the only card of that rank in the hand.
Follow suit if you can. The winner of a trick leads the next. At the end WOPR says CONTRACT MADE WITH n TRICKS or DOWN n, with the score.

controls.does: play that card from the hand whose turn it is
play a rank alone: the king in the suit led, or the only king in that hand
leave the deal and go back to WOPR

tips: Before you play to the first trick, count the sure tricks in both hands and compare them with the tricks the contract needs.
Lead toward your high cards. WOPR's defender who plays second always plays low, so with the ace and queen in dummy, lead a low card from your hand: if West holds the king, your queen wins.
In a suit contract, draw trumps early. WOPR's defenders trump your winners whenever they are out of a suit and their partner is not already winning the trick.
WOPR's opening lead is the top of a run of high cards, or the fourth-highest card of its longest suit outside trumps, so the lead tells you where the defenders are long.

screenshots.caption: The deal: CONTRACT 3NT BY SOUTH, dummy's North hand and your South hand a suit at a time, the auction, and West's opening 2D. The > marks dummy, which plays next.
East leads the 3S, South plays the JS and West covers with the QS; the > beside NORTH (DUMMY) says dummy plays next. LAST TRICK shows East's AD taking dummy's QD.
A club is refused because diamonds were led (SOUTH MUST FOLLOW SUIT: DIAMONDS.), then the KD and the AC take tricks: N-S 3, E-W 1.
